{{Short description|Conjecture that gravity must be the weakest force}}
{{Modern Physics}}
In [[theoretical physics]], the '''weak gravity conjecture''' ('''WGC''') is a [[conjecture]] regarding the strength [[gravity]] can have in a theory of [[quantum gravity]] relative to the gauge forces in that theory. It roughly states that gravity should be the weakest force in any consistent theory of quantum gravity.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Harlow |first1=Daniel |last2=Heidenreich |first2=Ben |last3=Reece |first3=Matthew |last4=Rudelius |first4=Tom |date=2023-09-06 |title=Weak gravity conjecture |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.95.035003 |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |language=en |volume=95 |issue=3 |article-number=035003 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.95.035003 |issn=0034-6861|arxiv=2201.08380 |bibcode=2023RvMP...95c5003H |osti=2420216 }}</ref> It was first proposed by [[Nima Arkani-Hamed]], [[Luboš Motl]], Alberto Nicolis, and [[Cumrun Vafa]] in 2007.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Arkani-Hamed |first1=Nima |last2=Motl |first2=Luboš |last3=Nicolis |first3=Alberto |last4=Vafa |first4=Cumrun |date=2007-06-15 |title=The string landscape, black holes and gravity as the weakest force |url=http://stacks.iop.org/1126-6708/2007/i=06/a=060?key=crossref.00fcba5a662b6db46cdc4d95e0d6eaee |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |volume=2007 |issue=6 |page=060 |doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2007/06/060 |issn=1029-8479|arxiv=hep-th/0601001 |bibcode=2007JHEP...06..060A }}</ref>

Gravity when compared to a [[U(1)]] gauge group interaction like [[electromagnetism]],{{explain|reason=What is this clause? It seems to set up "gravity" as the subject of a sentence but then throws it away in favour of the following "version"|date=December 2024}} the mildest version of the weak gravity conjecture implies that there exist an object with [[electric charge]] ''q'' and mass ''m'' such that

<math display="block">\frac{|q|}{m}\geq\left.\frac{|Q|}{M}\right|_{\text{ext}}</math>

where <math>\left.Q/M\right|_{\text{ext}}</math> is the charge-to-mass ratio of an arbitrary large [[black hole]].<ref name=":0" />

The conjecture was originally motivated by the fact that black holes should be able to decay. This insensitivity of black hole evaporation to its electric charge suggests that black holes can violate global symmetries and violate global charge conservation.<ref name=":0" />
